title: Full faithfulness of lisse restriction on a parameter-root limit
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a characteristic-$p$ field $k$ and a finite norm-topological extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Put $C_E(P)=C(P,E)$ for all profinite sets $P$ using all continuous maps, and use its pulled-back coefficient rings and internal modules [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Let $Y$ be a regular separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $B\to Y$ an affine etale chart, and $V(t_1\cdots t_r)$ a reduced strict normal crossings divisor whose branches on $B$ are precisely $V(t_d)$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. For an affine pro-etale $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to B$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], set
$$T=\operatorname{Spec}\left(\varinjlim_{(n,p)=1}R[x_{d,n}]_{1\le d\le r}/(x_{d,n}^n-t_d)_d\right),\qquad T^\circ=T\times_B B[1/(t_1\cdots t_r)].$$
The index is positive integers prime to $p$ ordered by divisibility, with $x_{d,n}\mapsto x_{d,m}^{m/n}$ for $n\mid m$. A lisse module means pro-etale locally finite free over the pulled-back $C_E$ [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. If $j:T^\circ\hookrightarrow T$ is the open inclusion, then for all finite-rank lisse $C_{E,T}$-modules $\mathcal N,\mathcal N'$ the restriction map
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{C_{E,T}}(\mathcal N,\mathcal N')\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{C_{E,T^\circ}}(j^*\mathcal N,j^*\mathcal N')$$
is a bijection. These bijections commute with pro-etale base change of $U$. They include the empty parameter list, rank zero, and the empty chart. No assertion about extending objects from $T^\circ$ is made.

proof.text: Write $B=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}S$ and $s=t_1\cdots t_r\in S$. An affine object $W=\operatorname{Spec}Q\to T$ of the small pro-etale site is weakly etale, by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Apply [lem-sfb-snc-root-limit-normal-charts] to the given chart and $A\to R$, and to $S\to Q$. It gives that $Q$ is normal and multiplication by $s$ on $Q$ is injective. The open $W^\circ=W\times_T T^\circ$ is $\operatorname{Spec}Q[1/s]$, directly by the localization universal property: a map factors through this inverse image exactly when the image of $s$ is invertible. No Noetherian assertion about $Q$ or $S$ is used.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the supplied-root-extension morphism argument; new geometric input

proof.text: The localization map $Q\to Q[1/s]$ is injective: a fraction $q/1$ is zero only if $s^Nq=0$, and repeated injectivity of multiplication by $s$ gives $q=0$. Since $s$ is a nonzerodivisor, $Q[1/s]$ embeds into the total ring of fractions of $Q$. Every idempotent $e$ in $Q[1/s]$ is integral over $Q$, satisfying $e^2-e=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-normal-ring-integrally-closed-total], $e$ is in $Q$; injectivity gives the idempotent equation there and uniqueness. Thus idempotents restrict bijectively. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent], this is precisely the inverse-image bijection $\operatorname{Clop}(W)\to\operatorname{Clop}(W^\circ)$, because $D(e)$ pulls back to $D(e/1)$. This also works for $Q=0$, when both spectra are empty.

Both $W$ and $W^\circ$ are affine, hence qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], and spectral by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral]. Apply [lem-sfb-spectral-clopen-component-homeomorphism] to their inclusion and the clopen bijection of step 2. It gives the normalized homeomorphism $h_W:\pi_0(W^\circ)\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi_0(W)$ with $h_Wq_{W^\circ}=q_Wj_W$, where each $q$ is the quotient map to connected components. This includes empty $W$.

source.place: Tag 0906, lemma-spectral-pi0, clopen criterion; Properties Tag 094L

proof.text: The norm topology of $E$ is totally disconnected: ultrametric balls are clopen and separate any two distinct points. Hence a continuous function from a connected space to $E$ is constant. For $a:|W^\circ|\to E$, write $a=\bar a q_{W^\circ}$. The quotient topology makes $\bar a$ continuous. Define $\widetilde a=\bar a h_W^{-1}q_W$. It is continuous and restricts to $a$. Conversely, factor any continuous function on $W$ through $q_W$ to see that this formula recovers it from its restriction. Thus actual restriction $C(|W|,E)\to C(|W^\circ|,E)$ is a bijection. It is a ring homomorphism by pointwise operations. For any $T$-map $v:Z\to W$ between affine site objects, restriction commutes with precomposition, so uniqueness gives $\widetilde{a\circ v^\circ}=\widetilde a\circ v$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12, continuous functions and components; extension formula supplied by agent

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-field-continuous-realization] for the totally disconnected normed field $E$. Its canonical ring-sheaf isomorphism identifies the actual pulled-back continuous coefficient sections on $W$ with $C(|W|,E)$ and those on $W^\circ$ with $C(|W^\circ|,E)$. The normalization on profinite test functions identifies their restriction with the restriction of step 4. Consequently $\Gamma(W,C_{E,T})\to\Gamma(W^\circ,C_{E,T^\circ})$ is bijective for every affine site object, naturally in that object. This is the all-continuous coefficient ring, not its discrete or locally constant substitute.

Choose a common pro-etale trivializing cover of $\mathcal N,\mathcal N'$ using [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]: take fibre products of their trivializing covers and refine by affine opens. The site covering rule of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] permits these refinements. On a member $W$ the modules are finite free of ranks $a,b$. By [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], a linear sheaf map is determined by the images of the $a$ standard basis sections; each is a $b$-tuple of coefficient sections. Conversely a $b\times a$ matrix of sections defines a linear map on every object over $W$ by restricting its entries and multiplying vectors. For a morphism on $T^\circ$, extend its matrix entries uniquely by step 5, obtaining a linear sheaf map on each $W$. This description also proves local uniqueness. Empty matrices handle either rank zero.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the supplied-root-extension morphism argument; elementary finite-free matrix argument

proof.text: On an overlap of two trivializing members, refine by affine opens. The two constructed maps have the same restriction to the punctured overlap, namely the given morphism. In either set of restricted bases their difference has zero matrix after restriction. Step 5 on each affine refinement forces every entry of that difference to vanish, so the maps agree. The sheaf gluing axiom, applied on every test object to the images of sections, glues them uniquely to a module morphism on $T$; additivity, scalar compatibility and naturality hold because they hold on this cover. The same local uniqueness shows that any two global maps with the same restriction agree. This proves surjectivity and injectivity of the required Hom restriction.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the supplied-root-extension morphism argument; sheaf gluing and uniqueness

proof.text: For a pro-etale base change $U'\to U$, put $T'=T\times_U U'$; the root-algebra presentation base changes to the stated presentation over $U'$, since tensor products commute with the displayed generators, relations and filtered colimit. Coefficients identify under pullback by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. Pullback carries the restriction of a map to the restriction of its pullback by the fibre-product projection equations. It carries local free bases to local free bases. Therefore the pullback of the unique extension and the extension of the pulled-back morphism restrict to the same map on $T'^\circ$; injectivity already proved for the new chart makes them equal. This is the requested base-change naturality. If $r=0$, $s=1$, $j$ is the identity and all formulas reduce to the identity. If the chart is empty, all Hom sets are singletons. The proof constructs only morphisms between the supplied modules.
